svg.text: The Archiv reading of the 1930s
Baeumler 1931 · Oehler · Härtle 1937
The published sentence it cannot accommodate
checkable at nietzschesource.org by siglum
1. The philosophy is a politics of the state
"Nietzsche the philosopher and politician":
will to power read as a programme for a
German state; recurrence dismissed as
"Egyptianism", a private religious feeling
Z I, "On the New Idol" (Za-I-Goetzen)
"State is the name of the coldest of all cold monsters."
EH, "Why I am so wise" §3 (restored 1969)
recurrence named "mein eigentlich abgründlicher Gedanke",
my properly abyssal thought — not a marginal one
2. "Rome against Judea" is a racial verdict
GM I:16 quoted as a war of peoples;
MA I 475's "stock-exchange Jew" clause
quoted alone (Oehler); six citations copied
from Härtle, one to a section that does not exist
GM I:16 · BGE 251 · MA I 475 read whole
"Rome against Judea" is "the symbol of this struggle" of
two valuations; Rome bows before "three Jews and one Jewess"
BGE 251: expel "the anti-Semitic screamers"; the Jews
"the strongest, purest, most tenacious race" in Europe
3. The Will to Power is the system
Baeumler's Kröner edition 1930: the 1906
compilation as the magnum opus; the published
books "a series of poses", the true Nietzsche
"only in the notes"
The notebooks themselves · the letters of 1887–88
NF-1888,14: four outlines in one season, none the book's;
to Deussen, 26 Nov 1888: the Revaluation "is finished"
as one book, the Antichrist · to Fritsch, 23 March 1887:
"no Jew among my friends. Admittedly no anti-Semites either"
each claim is answered by a sentence Nietzsche printed or wrote, cited by siglum; none of the answers makes him a liberal
